items.title: The pathway to internship success: how academic self-concept and engagement shape outcomes in higher education
items.abstract: Background Internships connect academic learning with workplace practice, yet the psychological process through which students' academic self-perceptions are associated with internship success remains insufficiently specified. This study examined whether multidimensional internship engagement statistically mediates the association between academic self-concept and internship outcomes. Methods A quantitative, multi-institutional, three-wave time-lagged survey was conducted with 522 undergraduate students from Chinese universities. Academic self-concept was assessed at internship entry, internship engagement at the internship midpoint, and internship outcomes after completion. Established instruments were adapted through forward translation, back-translation, expert review, and pilot testing. Confirmatory factor analysis, latent-variable structural equation modeling, 5,000-resample bootstrap mediation analysis, full-information maximum likelihood, robustness checks, and subgroup analyses were used. Results The hypothesized three-factor measurement model fit better than the two-factor and one-factor alternatives. The structural model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.958, TLI = 0.953, RMSEA = 0.034, and SRMR = 0.044). Academic self-concept was positively associated with internship engagement, and internship engagement was positively associated with internship outcomes. The indirect association through internship engagement was 0.249 (95% bootstrap confidence interval: 0.184 to 0.319). The proportion mediated was 50.6% (95% bootstrap confidence interval: 39.4% to 62.6%), and the direct association remained statistically significant. The pattern was stable across alternative specifications and exploratory subgroup analyses. Conclusion Internship engagement statistically accounted for part of the association between academic self-concept and internship outcomes. The findings support a theoretically ordered, but not causal, pathway in which students' academic self-evaluations are associated with stronger behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement during workplace learning.

items.title: The Potential Impacts of Artificial Intelligence on Preoperative Optimization and Predicting Risks of Morbidity and Mortality: A Narrative Focused Review
items.abstract: Preoperative optimization clinics enhance surgical outcomes by optimizing patients' health, reducing unnecessary tests, and minimizing cancellations. Artificial intelligence (AI) now promises to further advance these efforts by improving predictive modeling, automating risk assessments, and enabling personalized care strategies. AI models have shown particular strength in predicting postoperative complications, such as cardiovascular events. Tools like natural language processing (NLP) have also improved risk detection for conditions like alcohol misuse. The historical development of preoperative clinics-from Dr. J Alfred Lee's initial concept in 1949 to modern models like Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) and Anesthesia Preoperative Evaluation Clinic (APEC)-laid the groundwork for today's integration of electronic health records (EHRs) and decision-support systems, now evolving toward AI-driven care. Machine-learning algorithms have proven superior to traditional models for predicting postoperative anemia, opioid dependence, diabetes complications, and mortality risks, thus offering precise stratification and resource optimization. Specific applications include AI-assisted anemia management, penicillin allergy delabelling, and opioid use prediction after major surgeries. AI also enhances patient education through tools like ChatGPT and improves smoking cessation efforts using conversational AI. NLP has demonstrated better accuracy than standard International Classification of Disease (ICD) codes in identifying risky alcohol use (>2 standard drinks per day before surgery). However, barriers to widespread adoption include data privacy, algorithmic bias, and clinician skepticism. Future studies should focus on validating AI models across diverse populations and integrating AI recommendations within clinical workflows while adhering to evolving regulatory standards. Ultimately, AI's incorporation into preoperative assessments could significantly boost the efficiency and impact of clinic resources, potentially shifting outcomes more favorably by improving the slope of resource utilization versus patient outcome curves. Continued research and refinement are essential for AI to achieve its full potential in perioperative medicine.

items.title: The Remote Work Paradox: Why Flexibility Raises Retention—and Why Poor Design Destroys Collaboration
items.abstract: Remote work has become one of the most consequential and contested organizational changes of the modern workplace. Yet discussions about remote and hybrid work are often reduced to a binary disagreement between advocates of employee flexibility and leaders who prioritize office attendance. This working paper argues that the central question is not whether remote work universally succeeds or fails. The more useful question is which combinations of tasks, employees, managerial practices, communication systems, performance measures, and workplace arrangements allow remote work to produce sustainable value. The paper presents a practitioner-led narrative review of influential field experiments, observational studies, meta-analytic research, and international institutional evidence concerning remote and hybrid work. It examines six major outcome areas: employee productivity, retention, collaboration, professional learning, well-being, and equitable access to opportunity. The evidence indicates that the effects of remote work are heterogeneous rather than universally positive or negative.Research reviewed in the paper shows that remote work can increase measured performance in structured roles with observable outputs, limited task interdependence, and suitable working conditions. Hybrid arrangements can improve employee satisfaction and materially reduce voluntary turnover without reducing performance. Location flexibility can also broaden access to talent, reduce commuting burdens, support caregivers, and enable organizations to recruit beyond their immediate geographic markets. However, remote work can create important organizational costs when it is introduced without an appropriate operating system. Large-scale evidence suggests that firm-wide remote work can make collaboration networks more static and siloed, shift communication toward asynchronous channels, and reduce opportunities for spontaneous cross-team interaction. Distance can also weaken informal mentoring, slow the development of early-career employees, increase coordination costs, blur boundaries between professional and personal life, and expose weaknesses in management that physical proximity previously concealed.To reconcile these competing outcomes, the paper introduces the “remote work paradox”: the same flexibility that improves autonomy, retention, and focused individual work can simultaneously weaken collaboration, shared context, informal learning, and organizational connection. These effects are not mutually exclusive. A company may experience lower employee turnover while its internal collaboration network becomes narrower. An employee may complete more individual tasks while receiving less coaching and having fewer opportunities to form professionally valuable relationships. The paper proposes the REMOTE operating framework as a practical approach for designing and evaluating distributed work. The six dimensions of the framework are Role suitability, Expectation clarity, Managerial cadence, Output evidence, Team connection, and Equitable access. Together, these dimensions reposition remote work as an organizational-design challenge rather than a debate about employee location.Role suitability requires organizations to examine the actual tasks within each position and determine which activities benefit from quiet concentration, which require physical resources, and which depend on rapid coordination or tacit knowledge. Expectation clarity requires written outcomes, ownership, deadlines, quality standards, communication norms, and escalation procedures. Managerial cadence concerns the predictable systems through which managers provide coaching, feedback, prioritization, and workload review. Output evidence requires performance to be assessed through meaningful results rather than online visibility or digital activity. Team connection addresses trust, mentoring, weak ties, shared context, and cross-functional collaboration. Equitable access requires organizations to ensure that remote employees receive fair access to information, important assignments, feedback, sponsorship, compensation, and promotion opportunities. The paper also develops seven propositions that organizations can evaluate using their own operational data. These propositions address task suitability, coordinated hybrid schedules, employee retention, differences between experienced and early-career workers, the value of documentation, the influence of managerial capability, and the risk of proximity bias. The propositions are not presented as newly established causal findings. Instead, they translate the reviewed literature into testable expectations that organizations can use when conducting workplace-policy pilots. A five-stage implementation protocol is presented for employers. Organizations are encouraged to diagnose their work processes, design an explicit location model, pilot the model for a defined period, measure a balanced set of outcomes, and adapt the policy according to the evidence. Recommended measurements include productivity, work quality, cycle time, employee turnover, absenteeism, customer outcomes, collaboration patterns, onboarding progress, feedback latency, workload, employee experience, and equity across demographic and location groups. The paper concludes that remote work should be understood as an organizational technology whose value depends on complementary investments in management, documentation, communication, cybersecurity, job design, performance measurement, and inclusive employment practices. The strongest remote-work policy is neither the most permissive nor the most restrictive. It is the policy that makes productive work easier, learning faster, accountability clearer, collaboration more intentional, and professional opportunity more equitable.

items.title: The Reported Engagement with AI Level (REAL) Rating: A Framework for Disclosing Human-AI Collaboration
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has become increasingly incorporated into digital media and more generally into production workflows with which the public frequently interacts. Current provenance standards and disclosure methods frequently rely on binary categorizations, differentiating only between entirely human-authored and AI-generated content, or depend on technical watermarking that lacks user-facing clarity. However, there are very different risks and outcomes depending on the different uses of AI in the creation and consumption of end products. Therefore, we propose the Reported Engagement with AI Level (REAL) Rating framework which addresses these concerns by introducing a six-tier scale (Levels 0-5) that discloses the extent of AI involvement in both product creation and user experience. This paper details the structural methodology of the REAL Rating system and the specifics of its application across text, image, audio, video, and software products.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: The Role Of Artificial Intelligence In Transforming Financial Accounting And Tax Compliance
items.abstract: The role of artificial intelligence (AI) in transforming financial accounting and tax compliance is one of those areas that have become very intricate in terms of regulation. Based on the systematic review and synthesis of recent empirical research and industry surveys (2021–2026), the study evaluates how AI, including machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI, transforms essential accounting and tax processes. As follows, the implementation of AI technologies leads to efficiency gains, including 81% productivity increases and the enhancement of accuracy up to 98%. Companies using AI-powered compliance solutions attain the accuracy rate in fraud detection of more than 98%, while the processing time is reduced to less than a second. However, despite numerous benefits, there are still some challenges identified, including the lack of appropriate internal skills among 44% of respondents and low data readiness among 80% of respondents. Thus, the paper concludes that effective application of AI technologies is possible only through effective collaboration between humans and AI and appropriate governance, which requires significant investments into data infrastructure.

items.title: The Role Of Hospital Management In Improving Occupational Health And Safety (OHS) Program Compliance Among Non-Medical Staff At The West Java Provincial Occupational Health Regional Hospital
items.abstract: Hospitals present various occupational hazards, making the implementation of Hospital Occupational Health and Safety (OHS/K3RS) essential to protect all workers, including non-medical staff. This study aimed to analyze the role of hospital management in improving compliance with the OHS program among non-medical staff at the West Java Provincial Occupational Health Regional Hospital. A descriptive qualitative design was used with six informants selected through purposive sampling. The findings showed that management played an important role through the establishment of K3RS policies and the K3RS Team, confirmed by 50% of informants; provision of personal protective equipment (PPE) and OHS training, confirmed by 83.3%; and periodic program monitoring and evaluation, confirmed by 50%. Compliance among non-medical staff was generally good in PPE use, adherence to standard operating procedures, and participation in OHS activities, each confirmed by 50% of informants, although 66.7% reported variation in compliance across work units. All informants (100%) identified management commitment, policies, PPE, training, and unit-head support as enabling factors, while 66.7% reported barriers including budget limitations, limited K3RS human resources, PPE availability, workload, and inconsistent worker awareness. Management commitment therefore emerged as a key determinant, indicating the need to strengthen monitoring, OHS facilities, continuous training, and safety culture to sustain compliance.

items.title: The Sovereign GPU Dividend: A Reparative Levy on Artificial-Intelligence Inference and a Bond-Securitisation Mechanism to Fund Reparations for Transatlantic Chattel Slavery
items.abstract: The moral and legal case for reparations for transatlantic chattel slavery has advanced far ahead of any credible mechanism for paying them. Quantifications such as the 2023 Brattle Group report place the global liability at USD 100-131 trillion, with tens of trillions attributed to Britain alone - sums that no state can meet from general taxation. This paper proposes a funding mechanism that does not draw on the general taxpayer: a small ad valorem levy (3-5 per cent) on commercial artificial-intelligence inference - the sale of machine-generated "tokens" - collected at the billing layer of cloud and model-API providers, ring-fenced in statute, and securitised through the issue of long-dated sovereign Reparation Bonds. The mechanism deliberately mirrors, in reverse, the instrument through which Britain financed the GBP 20 million compensation paid to slave owners under the Slavery Abolition Act 1833: a debt serviced from general taxation across generations, whose successor instruments were not redeemed until February 2015, so that descendants of the enslaved were themselves among the taxpayers who serviced it. We model three revenue scenarios against current market data and show that the levy could realistically service USD 40 billion to USD 1 trillion of reparations bonds over the coming decade, scaling automatically with the growth of the AI economy. We position the proposal against the emerging token-tax literature and argue that its contribution is the ring-fencing of AI-derived fiscal capacity to a specific historical liability: the unpaid labour debt of slavery, settled by the automated labour that now substitutes for human work. The mechanism is presented as a credible first instalment and a scalable architecture, not a full settlement. Note on version 6 (October 2026): this version corrects the United Kingdom liability figure given in earlier versions, which was a sterling conversion of a single scenario in the Brattle report presented as the report's own figure, and removes a levy rate attributed to a named executive that could not be verified against a primary source. It also adds sections on the 1833 parliamentary debates and on Jamaica's 2026 petition to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council. The corrections are set out in full in the "Note on this version" section at the front of the paper.

items.title: Theoretical Foundations of the Relationship between Labor Productivity and Wage
items.abstract: Issues concerning the relationship between productivity and wages are directly linked to attempts to assess the outcomes of human labor. As the intellectual component of labor increases and the share of services grows, the challenge of quantifying labor becomes increasingly acute. This article examines the evolution of theoretical approaches to understanding productivity and wages — from the mercantilists and the classical school to the new neoclassical synthesis. The study reveals a trend toward an increasing role of the human factor and greater attention to intrinsic motivation when examining the relationship between labor productivity and wages. The contemporary understanding of the productivity–wage nexus is gradually moving away from purely market-based concepts toward incorporating the socio-psychological dimensions of labor relations. The findings may be used to develop recommendations for improving the remuneration system in the Russian Federation.

items.title: Theories and Concepts of Occupational Health and Safety
items.abstract: The field of Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) is multidisciplinary in nature and crosscuts sectors, ensuring the safety and health of workers, including their well-being, to improve productivity through the identification and control of hazards at workplweaces. The theoretical and conceptual perspectives of OH&S have been explored in this chapter, stressing the responses to global catastrophic accidents and the effect of globalisation on OH&S and illustrating definitions advanced by various institutions and scholars. Significant to OH&S, the chapter highlights the integration of occupational health, safety management systems, and risk management practices to enhance safe workplaces and organisational culture positively. The discussions delve deeper into accident causation theories, such as Heinrich’s work and succeeding theories that attribute accidents to unsafe conditions, human error, organisational factors, and random events. The cost of accidents through economic, social, and moral perspective is analysed, differentiating direct and indirect impacts on workers, employers, and the communities. Further, tangible and intangible benefits of investing in OH&S have been shown to enhance effective management and lessen accident occurrence, enhance employee well-being, and improve the reputation of an organisation while adding to sustainable competitiveness. In essence, OH&S is outlined to be a human-centric and technical field fundamental to a more resilient and progressive firm and society.

items.title: Time Series Forecasting Benchmarks Need Scenario-Grounded Stress Testing
items.abstract: Time series forecasting (TSF) increasingly drives decisions in transportation, energy, finance, healthcare, and infrastructure, yet current evaluation remains overly narrow: standard benchmarks reward low held-out error, while robustness studies typically reduce failure to Gaussian noise, random masking, or bounded adversarial perturbations. This obscures the real failure modes of deployed forecasting systems. Input-side anomalies are not merely noisier inputs: they often reflect structured events that alter temporal dynamics, break cross-variable dependencies, induce regime shifts, or propagate from faulty sensors to downstream decisions. These semantic, causal, and system-level failures cannot be faithfully captured by i.i.d. perturbations alone. The rise of TSF foundation models makes this evaluation gap more urgent, as unauditable pretraining corpora make held-out generalization increasingly unreliable. We therefore advocate scenario-grounded stress testing. Each test instance should include historical inputs and future targets, together with a semantic scenario, an explicit failure operator, and a measurable difficulty level. This shift makes evaluation interpretable, attributable, and deployment-relevant and friendly, enabling the community to ask not only which model is accurate, but under what conditions it fails and why.

items.title: Toward SLM-based agentic task-tool intent matching
items.abstract: Tool-equipped AI agents use tool calls to access data and act on external systems. Horizontal growth of agentic systems increases the number of these interactions, and further motivates the need for automated, per-call oversight that can operate at low latency and/or on-prem. Conventional authorization schemes can determine whether an agent is allowed to invoke a tool, but cannot assess the agent's underlying cognition, specifically, whether the tool selection represents a logical, relevant step toward satisfying the intent of the task or not. Consequently, an allowed call may still deviate from the task's intent: a rogue agent might deviate the calls or nudge other agents to make a combination of calls that would not align with the intent of the task. Therefore, every call needs to be verified. In this study we investigate the applicability of Small Language Models (SLMs) to this purpose: an SLM functions as a task-tool relevance classifier that evaluates every selected tool independently against the assigned task and returns a relevance signal for downstream enforcement. Equipped with a novel dataset with multi-tool tasks whose required tools span distinct Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, we used prompt-optimization, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning through GRPO to optimize and specialize SLMs.

items.title: Traffic boardgames and played mobilities
items.abstract: In this article, we examine ten traffic‑themed boardgames published in Finland between the 1950s and 1970s. We introduce our novel concept of played mobilities as an analytical category of imagined mobilities. The concept of played mobilities refers to the active and performative manners of imagining traffic within a framework suggested by any game but also to the potential ways a player can stretch and break a game’s established rules. Our study demonstrates how traffic games were specifically used to teach children and young people about how to behave within a traffic system that was primarily dictated by automobility. These games’ introduction was driven by an increase in the number of cars, changes in traffic regulations, and the rise in traffic accidents in Finland. However, these games also inspired an understanding of traffic as something playable and a highly individualist notion of participating in traffic. During the 1970s, the games increasingly acknowledged other forms of mobility as well. At the same time, their depictions of traffic shifted from futuristic sociotechnical imaginaries towards more realistic traffic scenarios and environments as the car-centric traffic system had, by then, transformed into a mundane aspect of everyday life for most Finns.

items.title: Trajectory-Derived Confidence for Reliable, Resource-Aware Clinical Text-to-SQL Agents
items.abstract: LLM agents for clinical text-to-SQL applications reason autonomously over multiple steps but cannot assess whether their own reasoning or outputs can be trusted. In high leverage applications such as healthcare, this presents a critical risk where system mistakes can be costly. These reliability failures are also resource failures: an incorrect reasoning trajectory spends computation budget on outputs that must be discarded. We introduce Sentinel, a trajectory-derived, classifier-based confidence layer that analyzes an agent's reasoning, code and database outputs to decide at three points whether to stop: refusing unanswerable questions before the agent runs, halting doomed trajectories mid-run, and withholding untrustworthy answers at delivery. Here, utilizing Chow's rule, we optimize decisions under the EHRSQL shared task's Reliability Score, which penalizes incorrect answers given a utility weighting, and find on the benchmark EHRSQL that Sentinel raises this score from +0.08 to +0.24 when mistakes have a low utility weighting, well above the +0.03 earned by refusing every question, with delivered-answer accuracy rising from 54% to 69% as coverage falls from 84% to 55%. At higher stakes the agents we test rarely answer reliably enough to deliver, and Sentinel detects this on its own, abstaining to that same +0.03 where the unmonitored agent scores -3.02. The same stopping decisions cut computation: at low stakes, where the system still answers, Sentinel eliminates 13-28% of agent steps at little or no reliability cost.

items.title: Transformasi Digital dalam Akuntansi Keuangan: Systematic Literature Review Menggunakan Pendekatan PRISMA
items.abstract: Aim: This study aims to analyze the development of digital transformation in financial accounting, identify dominant technologies and research themes, and explore research gaps in the field of digital transformation in financial accounting. Method: This study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. The data consist of scientific articles obtained from Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Emerald Insight, Google Scholar, and other scholarly sources. A total of 18 articles published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using content analysis with a thematic analysis approach. Results: The findings indicate that blockchain is the most dominant technology in the transformation of financial accounting due to its contribution to transparency, accountability, financial reporting quality, and fraud mitigation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation also play important roles in improving the efficiency of accounting and auditing processes and supporting data-driven decision-making. However, existing research remains largely dominated by conceptual and literature-based studies, while empirical research examining the implementation of digital technologies in accounting practices remains relatively limited. Conclusion/Novelty/Implications: The novelty of this study lies in systematically mapping dominant technologies and research themes while identifying empirical research gaps. The findings imply that future research should integrate technology, governance, regulation, cybersecurity, and human resource competencies to support effective and sustainable digital transformation in financial accounting.

items.abstract: In the Industrial Revolution 4.0 era, the limitation of conventional marketing reach and low adoption of digital technology pose major challenges to cooperative sustainability. Koperasi Serba Usaha (KSU) Rakyat Sejahtera Abadi (Raja) Bekasi possesses strong asset potential of IDR 2.5 billion with 450 active members. However, the cooperative faces stagnant member growth (<5% annually) with 70% of members aged over 45, primarily due to 100% reliance on conventional marketing strategies (zero digital content). This Community Service (PkM) project aims to boost the digital capacity of cooperative managers and members through training in business social media account setup, digital target audience mapping, and short video content creation on TikTok integrated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools. The execution methods consisted of preparation (assessment), implementation (lectures, discussions, and hands-on practical guidance), and evaluation. Held on April 19, 2026, in Rawalumbu, Bekasi City, the event engaged 60 participants. The results demonstrated a significant enhancement in participants' hard skills regarding storyboard creation, promotional video production for savings and loan products, and TikTok algorithm optimization. This initiative successfully laid a sustainable digital transformation foundation for KSU Raja to expand market reach and attract younger generation.

items.title: Trust, Ethics, and Brand Reputation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: In the AI era, trust, ethics, and brand reputation converge in governance, making them inseparable. This chapter examines that claim through four cases: the UAE's state-led AI strategy, the EU's rights-based regulatory model, and the contrasting trajectories of Anthropic and OpenAI. It argues that reputational credibility in AI depends less on innovation narratives or ethical branding than on whether ethical claims rest on visible, contestable, and durable institutional arrangements. To clarify this, it proposes a reputational architecture of trust built on structural, relational, and procedural dimensions. It also shows how governance quality reaches consumers through media coverage, recourse mechanisms, reviews, trust marks, and employee word of mouth. The chapter concludes that governance is not a compliance add-on but a central condition of legitimate innovation.

items.abstract: At the close of the twentieth century, human semantic memory was thought to be organized around dedicated, domain-specific modules operating independently of one another and of perception, action, and much of language. The intervening years have marked a transition toward a more holistic view in which semantics emerges from learned mappings among sensory, motor, and language representations, with recent work beginning to integrate semantic representation with theories of cognitive control and attention. This article reviews the reasons for this remarkable change in perspective, provides a snapshot of our current understanding of semantics in the mind and brain, and considers how this understanding may change in light of new innovations in artificial intelligence.

items.title: UNLEASHING HARMONIOUS GREEN PASSION IN HOSPITALITY ENTERPRISES: A MODERATED-MEDIATED ROLE OF PRO-ENVIRONMENTAL BEHAVIOR AND GREEN ORGANIZATIONAL CLIMATE
items.abstract: Environmental sustainability in the hospitality sector increasingly depends on the alignment between employees’ intrinsic motivations, supportive organizational contexts, and environmentally responsible behaviors. Drawing on SelfDetermination Theory, this study examines how Harmonious Green Passion influences environmental performance in Egypt’s five-star hotels, focusing on the mediating role of pro-environmental behavior and the moderating effect of green organizational climate. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 402 hotel employees and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The findings demonstrate that Harmonious Green Passion positively influences both proenvironmental behavior and environmental performance, while pro-environmental behavior partially mediates the relationship between Harmonious Green Passion and environmental performance. Furthermore, green organizational climate significantly strengthens the positive relationship between Harmonious Green Passion and pro-environmental behavior, consequently reinforcing its indirect effect on environmental performance. These findings extend Self-Determination Theory by elucidating a motivation–behavior–performance mechanism through which employees’ environmentally oriented passion translates into organizational outcomes, while demonstrating that this process is contingent upon contextual organizational conditions. Practically, the findings suggest that hotel managers should cultivate supportive green organizational climates, encourage employees’ intrinsic environmental motivation, and facilitate pro-environmental behaviors through appropriate organizational practices. Such efforts can strengthen employees’ environmental engagement and contribute to improved environmental performance, offering hospitality organizations a pathway toward more sustainable operations and long-term environmental value creation.

items.title: Use of AI tools among allied healthcare students: Academic integrity, online learning integrity, and nomophobia as predictors
items.abstract: The swift convergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), online instruction, and mobile dependence has transformed higher education, introducing both innovations and ethical problems for allied health training. Although individual studies on AI adoption, digital ethics, and device dependence exist, a significant empirical gap remains regarding how psychological reliance on mobile devices (nomophobia) and virtual-specific ethics jointly drive GenAI adoption among healthcare students, where ethical lapses directly impact clinical competence. To address this gap, this study examined the predictive roles of academic integrity, online learning integrity, and nomophobia in the use of AI tools among allied healthcare students at a higher education institution. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional design, the researchers collected data via convenience sampling among 300 full-time allied health students in Central Luzon, Philippines. The study used four research tools to gather pertinent data for the investigation, including an online survey administered during the second semester of the 2025-2026 academic year. Both descriptive and inferential statistics were employed using SPSS 23. Descriptive results showed high academic integrity, moderate AI usage and nomophobia, but low online learning integrity. Correlation analyses showed that AI tool use was positively associated with online learning integrity, nomophobia, and academic integrity. Multiple linear regression demonstrated that the model significantly predicted AI usage. Online learning integrity was the strongest predictor, followed by academic integrity and nomophobia. These results show that ethical digital engagement and mobile connectedness actively propel AI integration; ultimately, achieving SDG 4 objectives within healthcare education requires moving beyond prohibitive policies toward anticipatory digital governance, robust AI literacy, and ethical models that prepare future professionals for a digitally driven medical environment.

items.title: Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation to Support Parameter-Specific Takeover Request Personalization in Automated Driving
items.abstract: Conditionally automated vehicles still require drivers to retake control when automation reaches its operational limits, so takeover request (TOR) design remains a safety concern. This study developed and evaluated a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that uses a large language model (LLM) to produce parameter-specific, literature-grounded TOR plans. Two literature corpora on takeover factors and alert modality served as the knowledge base, and a structured situation object represented driver traits, driver state, non-driving-related tasks, and driving scenario conditions. The system generated TOR plans across 10 parameter categories for 40 persona-scenario combinations. Several TOR parameters varied with takeover-relevant inputs in the generated test set, and modality recommendations changed according to the sensory impairments described in the situation object. These preliminary results suggest that RAG-based LLMs may support parameter-specific TOR personalization in automated driving.

items.title: Using sensor and self-reported data to understand fatigue within the massage therapy profession
items.abstract: This exploratory study examined the relationship between the massage modalities used, the length of the massage treatment, and the areas of the body massaged on the perceived self-reported effort level and muscular fatigue as well as the ergonomic sensor data for average composite risk score and average fatigue risk score. Participants completed their normal routine of massages while wearing sensors: watch placed on the upper arm to collect physiological data; GoX ® sensor placed on the dominant upper arm and back of the shirt to collect ergonomic data. Participants performed massages in their regular clinic, following their normal treatment plan. Following each session, a survey was completed about the massage treatment, including areas massaged, techniques used and self-reported effort and muscle fatigue. Mean self-reported effort level was 10.71± 2.40, light level on the Borg Scale. Mean self-reported muscular fatigue level was 2.69 ± 0.75, light activity on the RPE scale. Length of time of the massage session was not a strong indicator of subjective or objective measures. No one technique provided an increased risk of fatigue. This exploratory study gave a snapshot into fatigue and risks for work-related musculoskeletal disorders in massage therapists while practicing in their normal clinical setting.

items.title: Validation of a Questionnaire to Explore Artificial Intelligence Use Among Upper-Secondary and Higher Education Teachers
items.abstract: Research on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education has shifted from students to teachers, yet available teacher instruments rest on technology acceptance models, professional knowledge frameworks, or AI literacy, and none articulates dispositional conditions, teaching activities, and contextual consequences within a single functional logic. This study extends to teachers an instrument previously validated with students and grounded in Functional Behavior Analysis and the Interbehavioral Model of Didactic Performance. Participants were 233 Mexican upper-secondary and higher education teachers (mean age 47.22 years, SD = 10.44). The study is strictly psychometric in scope: it reports initial reliability and internal structure evidence, not a profile of teacher practice. Reliability was estimated with Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega with bootstrap confidence intervals, and the number of components was determined through Horn’s parallel analysis. Alpha coefficients ranged from 0.703 to 0.957 (omega, 0.755 to 0.962). The benefits dimension split into two uncorrelated components, pedagogical benefits (α = 0.953) and risks to academic integrity (α = 0.771). Domains of didactic performance proved unidimensional (63.0% of variance); the consequences dimension behaved as a formative index rather than a reflective scale; and the dispositional dimension failed to separate individual from contextual variables and required redesign. A second-order analysis yielded two orthogonal axes, favourable pedagogical orientation and risk recognition, on which four quadrants are described for illustrative purposes only. The instrument discriminates across self-reported frequency of AI use. Because components were extracted from Pearson correlations on ordinal items in a single convenience sample, the structure reported here is provisional and requires confirmation with polychoric matrices and robust estimators on an independent sample.

items.title: Validation of an Occupational Health and Safety Performance Management Framework for Small-Scale Contractors in Developing Countries
items.abstract: The chapter expounds on the validation of the occupational health and safety (OH&S) performance management framework for small-scale contractors (SSCs) in developing countries using the Delphi approach. This method confirms the relevance of the framework’s elements where there is limited empirical data, in a more structured consensus-building process. A group of 11 experts who participated in two iterative rounds of questionnaires took part in the study based on their professional experience, education, and involvement in the industry. To reduce bias and allow for reliable judgement, the validation process was anonymous, with iterative feedback and statistical measures. The critical constructs that reached consensus include management strategy, finance, employee involvement, training, hazard identification, continuous improvement, employee wellbeing, and provision of OH&S services. A 60% agreement threshold was attained by experts who rated the likelihood and impact of these elements as acceptable. The framework validates that employee wellbeing and organisational safety culture positively influence accident reduction. The chapter further underscores the credibility of the framework in the context of SSCs in Zambia as it offers a structured approach to improve OH&S performance that aligns with international standards and best practices.

items.title: VenusRL: A Fully Disaggregated Agentic RL System with Priority Scheduling and Scalable Interaction
items.abstract: Agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) trains LLM agents through multi-turn interactions with external tool environments. Its multi-turn nature exposes two system-level bottlenecks unaddressed by existing agentic RL frameworks. First, end-to-end training throughput is constrained by the slowest trajectories to complete, yet optimizing per-GPU utilization alone scatters rollout progress across many groups, delaying the completion of enough groups to unblock the next training step. Second, tool sandboxes are statically over-provisioned by their declared memory ceilings, leaving most physical memory stranded while replicating near-identical state across sandboxes launched from the same prompt. We present VenusRL, a fully disaggregated agentic RL system that addresses both bottlenecks. VenusRL's priority-aware action scheduler uses length-prediction heuristics to identify sample groups whose completion is most likely to unblock the next training step, and pushes them ahead of others across batch admission, KV Cache residency, and cross-worker request orchestration. VenusRL's environment resource manager combines a memory-aware admission threshold with a template-keyed page-sharing pool, packing more sandboxes per node while preserving strict memory isolation via write-protected page table entry aliasing and copy-on-write. Across representative agentic RL workloads, VenusRL achieves up to 4.24x end-to-end training speedup over state-of-the-art baselines and reduces environment cost by up to 89%.

items.title: Visión artificial para la detección de plagas en cultivos de tomate: revisión sistemática de la literatura
items.abstract: Phytosanitary monitoring is an essential activity for reducing production losses caused by pests in tomato crops grown under protected agriculture conditions. In recent years, computer vision and deep learning methods have gained relevance as tools capable of automating agricultural image detection and analysis processes. Despite these advances, there is still a need to determine which techniques have been used, under what conditions they have been evaluated, and what performance they have reported, particularly in protected agriculture and small-scale production contexts. This study aims to examine research published on these technologies and assess their potential incorporation into participatory agricultural monitoring schemes. To this end, a systematic review of scientific literature published between 2020 and 2026 was conducted following the methodological guidelines proposed by Kitchenham. The review was developed through the stages of planning, study search and selection, and information synthesis, considering previously established inclusion and exclusion criteria. As a result, fifty studies related to image processing, artificial intelligence, and phytosanitary monitoring were selected and analyzed. Among the main findings of the review, several studies reported high-performance levels for deep learning models in tasks involving the automatic identification of symptoms associated with pests and other crop-related conditions. The synthesis identified the main techniques, data, application contexts, and reported performance levels, providing reference elements for assessing their potential incorporation into participatory agricultural monitoring schemes.

items.title: Weave Forcing: Compositional Memory Routing for Interactive Long Video Generation
items.abstract: Recent advances in autoregressive video generation have improved temporal consistency over extended durations, yet interactive storytelling requires more than continuous scene extension: a new shot may combine characters and backgrounds from different historical shots. Whole prompt retrieval can overlook the distinct reference needs of individual components, while directly combining all historical memories may introduce unrelated visual content. To address these problems, we present Weave Forcing, a training-free framework for compositional memory reuse in interactive long video generation. First, we use an LLM for semantic slot routing to decompose user prompts into character and background descriptions and explicitly select suitable historical references for each component. To isolate the required content, masked memory weaving uses contrasting attention maps conditioned on semantic slots to construct refined semantic masks, selectively exposing relevant tokens from compressed historical KV memories to guide the generation of the current shot. We further introduce coverage adaptive RoPE to adjust temporal offsets and memory retention according to no, partial, or full reference coverage, addressing visual artifacts observed when incomplete historical references are positioned close to the current generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Weave Forcing improves cross-shot subject and background consistency while maintaining competitive visual quality and text alignment.

items.title: WebUIProof: Benchmarking WebUI Code Generators with UI-Agent Execution Harness
items.abstract: Evaluating WebUI code generation at scale is difficult: outputs may compile and look plausible yet fail under user interaction, and prior benchmarks largely rely on free-form prompts with static checks (build success, screenshots) that miss functional correctness. We introduce WebUIProof, an execution-oriented benchmark that provides structured specifications and dense, executable interaction tests for WebUI generation across two task families: general WebUIs (e.g., dashboards, game, interactive tools) and 3D interactive simulation (e.g., particle/galaxy systems, physics dynamics). WebUIProof includes a UI-agent harness that runs executable interaction tests in a headless browser using an iterative plan--act--observe loop: it locates DOM elements, performs actions, observes resulting UI/DOM changes, and checks the specified assertions. We evaluate across eight commercial LLMs and observe frequent failures on interaction-based requirements even when pages render successfully, especially on 3D simulation interfaces. Finally, we show the UI-agent harness can provide outcome-level training signals. Training compact models (e.g., Qwen2.5 14B and MIMO 7B) with RL rewards derived from executable interaction tests improves functional completion while reducing build failures.

items.title: What Is Lost in Post-Training? Default Collapse and the Loss of In-Context Steerability Across Diverse Perspectives
items.abstract: AI models serving a heterogeneous population must act on the principles appropriate to each user and context. While post-training has been shown to narrow the views large language models express, prior work has focused on default behavior rather than the ability to adapt to in-context information. We show that post-training also degrades a model's ability to be steered in-context toward perspectives it was not trained to favor. In controlled experiments, we fine-tune models toward one side of cultural-value disagreements and evaluate checkpoints throughout training. The trained side becomes increasingly dominant in ordinary use, while the ability to recognize and faithfully enact the opposing view declines. These findings point to a tension between prioritizing a single set of values and preserving the technical capacity needed to serve diverse stakeholders. Finally, we propose and analyze an alternative objective that maximizes reward subject to a prescribed distribution over expressed perspectives, and present stance-distribution matching as a practical implementation.

items.title: When Does Synthetic Relational Data Teach Models to Use Relations? Tracing Predictive Structure from Pretraining Data to Model Behavior
items.abstract: Relational foundation models are increasingly pretrained on synthetic databases, yet downstream benchmarks reveal little about why one synthetic corpus produces a better model than another. In particular, strong performance may arise from realistic row-level statistics without the model ever learning to use relational structure. We study this as a data-attribution problem: which property of synthetic pretraining data induces relational computation? Using four Relational Transformer checkpoints trained with the same architecture, initialization, objective, and compute budget on corpora produced by four relational data generators, we trace a measurable property of the data to learned computation and downstream behavior. We hypothesize that relational mechanisms emerge when cross-table information is predictively necessary for the masked-cell pretraining objective. RelDiff exhibits by far the largest predictive gain from foreign-key-linked parents, and its corresponding model is uniquely sensitive to foreign-key interventions on unseen databases. This dependence survives a random-initialization control, grows monotonically with the fraction of corrupted links, and localizes to a serial cross-table pathway. Finally, disrupting the same mechanism during downstream inference removes RelDiff's advantage on relational tasks while leaving structure-insensitive models nearly unchanged. These results connect a property of synthetic training data to a learned mechanism and, through intervention, to downstream behavior.

items.title: When Numbers Start Talking: Numerical Signalling and Strategic Behaviour Among LLMs
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents increasingly operate in multi-agent systems (MAS) characterised by strategic interaction. However, little is known about whether, and to what extent, different types of messages affect the outcomes of strategic games. By investigating AI agents based on four popular LLMs, playing four games with different cooperation equilibria, we study whether messages of different kinds (natural language, numerical signals, or random sequences) significantly modify the levels of cooperation in each game, also depending on the agents' assigned personalities. We observe that structured messages alter the final payoffs for most games and LLMs, but without a predictable pattern; this challenges the assumption that AI agents can converge to stable equilibria regardless of additional capabilities. Moreover, we observe that agent-generated numerical messages depart from randomness, most strongly and consistently when agents are explicitly instructed to communicate; however, they introduce an additional interpretability challenge, as their symbol distributions are mostly associated with the payoff structure and typically become more concentrated with repetition, but are overall difficult for humans to interpret. Monitoring for coordination of AI agents through restricted channels should thus prioritise message-level fingerprints, which generalise across models, over behavioural decisions, which do not.

items.title: Writerslogic at PAN 2026: Process over Content for Robust Detection under Domain Shift
items.abstract: We describe the Writerslogic systems for three PAN at CLEF 2026 shared tasks (Reasoning Trajectory Detection, Voight-Kampff Generative AI Detection, and Multi-Author Writing Style Analysis), unified by a shared analytical framework: feature robustness under distribution shift is governed by support overlap between training and test distributions, not by training-set effect size. This yields a taxonomy (domain-anchored, domain-portable, domain-invariant) that explains why generator-specific features die under domain shift while vocabulary fingerprints (hapax ratio, Yule's K, Heaps' exponent), compression measures, and character n-grams survive. On Reasoning Trajectory Detection, where training was entirely mathematics and 84 percent of test was unseen domains, the framework guided system design to 1st place in source detection (0.85 macro F1 via Opus-Sonnet agreement) and 3rd place in safety classification (0.66 macro F1 via query-refusal decomposition). For Voight-Kampff, we built a calibrated ensemble of DeBERTa-v2 (ONNX), multi-seed LightGBM with 44 domain-portable stylometric features, and SVM on n-gram TF-IDF, combined via learned stacking with isotonic calibration; the best configuration achieved 0.891 on the PAN 2026 test set with balanced sub-metrics (0.853 to 0.902 across all evaluation dimensions). For Multi-Author Writing Style Analysis, we describe a system fusing spectral clustering over character n-gram similarity graphs, normalized compression distance for local boundary detection, and SmolLM-135M perplexity for neural change-point detection; a platform mix-up meant our run never reached the official evaluation, so we report the design and its a priori predictions. Across all three tasks, features measuring generation process properties are designed to outperform features measuring generated content properties under domain shift.

items.title: Writerslogic at the CLEF 2026 SimpleText Track: Multi-Candidate LLM Simplification and Stacked Complexity Spotting
items.abstract: We describe the Writerslogic team's participation in the CLEF 2026 SimpleText shared task, addressing Task 1 (text simplification) and Task 2 (complexity spotting). For Task 1, we develop a multi-candidate generation pipeline using GPT-4o-mini that produces five simplification candidates per sentence at varying temperatures, then selects the best candidate using a reference-free scoring heuristic that rewards compression, source word retention, Cochrane Plain Language Summary vocabulary usage, and lexical simplicity. On Task 1.1 (sentence-level simplification), our Claude Sonnet 4 submission achieves SARI 47.43 and BLEU 14.21, the top-ranked sentence-level system (3rd on the combined Task 1 leaderboard, behind two document-level submissions). For Task 2, we fine-tune a DeBERTa-v3-large NLI model on 350K labeled (source, sentence) pairs, framing hallucination detection as natural language inference. The model reads the most relevant source sentence as premise and the candidate as hypothesis, directly learning to distinguish grounded from hallucinated content. On Task 2.1 (binary overgeneration identification), our fine-tuned DeBERTa system achieves 0.8081 document-level macro F1 (0.8085 in our best ensemble), the top-ranked entry within the identification track and 2nd among teams overall, behind AIIR Lab (0.8197). On Task 2.2 (multi-class error classification), our best submission reaches 0.804 multiclass accuracy, ranking 2nd among unique teams behind AIIR Lab (0.827). We evaluate both tasks on English and multilingual biomedical text from Cochrane systematic reviews.

items.title: YOLO-BASED SYSTEMS FOR DETECTING EXPLOSIVE REMNANTS OF WAR: A REVIEW FOR HUMANITARIAN DEMINING
items.abstract: Relevance. Humanitarian demining remains a critical safety challenge because explosive remnants of war, landmines, and unexploded ordnance continue to endanger civilians and hinder post-conflict recovery. In this context, artificial intelligence and computer vision are increasingly used to support hazardous-object detection in UAVs-based survey operations. The purpose of this paper is to synthesize contemporary approaches to the detection of landmines, unexploded ordnance, and other explosive remnants of war, and to define the role of YOLO models in an integrated technological pipeline for surveying hazardous areas. The object of the review is technological solutions for detecting hazardous objects using UAVs, sensor systems, geoinformation technologies, and YOLO-family models. The subject of the paper is the application of YOLO-based systems in integrated pipelines for localizing potential explosive objects from visual and spectral data. Research results. The review shows that modern approaches combine ground-penetrating radar, magnetometry, thermal sensing, multispectral imaging, hyperspectral imaging, UAV-based inspection, GIS platforms, and edge/cloud architectures. YOLO demonstrates strong potential for rapid localization of visually or spectrally expressed indicators of hazardous objects, especially when combined with other sensing modalities. Conclusions. At the same time, YOLO cannot serve as the sole basis for declaring an area safe. Its use is constrained by small target size, camouflage, domain shift, limited annotated datasets, and the high cost of false negatives. Therefore, YOLO-based detection should be treated as one component of a multisensor, human-supervised decision-support system.

items.title: ZeroMAG: Zero-Shot Multimodal Adapter Generation for Plug-and-Play EEG Foundation Models
items.abstract: EEG foundation models (EFMs) capture reusable knowledge from large-scale EEG data, while many EEG recordings also include companion physiological signals that provide complementary information beyond the EEG-only interface. The challenge is to preserve this pretrained knowledge while extending the EFM to heterogeneous multimodal recordings through an adaptation inferred from unlabeled target data. We introduce ZeroMAG, a zero-shot multimodal adapter generation framework that extends a frozen EEG encoder and prediction head using unlabeled target recordings, without target labels or target-side optimization. The target datasets are held out from all model training and selection in the ZeroMAG pipeline. ZeroMAG organizes companion modalities around a configuration-invariant adapter, constructs a modality-subject-task condition from unlabeled recordings and task context, and generates adapter weights in a function-constrained latent space learned from source adapters. Across six held-out target datasets and three EFM backbones, ZeroMAG improves balanced accuracy by 7.22 percentage points over EEG-only inference and 4.89 points over direct weight regression, while coming within 0.50 points of supervised multimodal adaptation on average. Ablations further show that removing functional supervision from either representation learning or conditional generation degrades generated-adapter performance, confirming the contribution of both components.

items.abstract: The article examines non-standard forms of employment and outlines their legal regulation through the lens of the International Labour Organization’s activities. It is noted that international labour standards represent a consolidated embodiment—within universal and regional legal instruments—of best practices, taking into account existing legal regulatory systems and the practical experience of states in protecting workers’ labour and social rights. At the same time, harmonizing national legislation with international standards, particularly the provisions of the European Social Charter, facilitates Ukraine’s European integration and the development of civilized labour relations. International legal regulation plays a pivotal role in protecting workers’ rights by establishing minimum standards that adapt to global challenges. The International Labour Organization serves as the primary coordinator and developer of these standards, creating universal rules that member states implement into their national legislation. As a member of the ILO, Ukraine has ratified a number of key conventions, aligning its labor legislation with European and international standards. It is emphasized that the use of non-standard employment arrangements helps, on the one hand, to optimize the management and allocation of employer costs and, on the other, to accommodate the individual needs of the worker and the specific nature of their work. At the same time, the negative consequences of the expanding use of atypical employment cannot be overlooked. In particular, there is a risk of employers abusing their authority regarding the provision of labor and social guarantees, wage payments, occupational health and safety, and the tracking of working hours. The conclusion is drawn that the regulation of atypical forms of employment is a key focus of both European and Ukrainian legislation. The rapid development of the digital economy necessitates the continuous improvement of the legal framework to prevent instability in the labor sphere and ensure the protection of citizens’ social and labor guarantees. In assessing the international legal regulation of atypical forms of employment, it must be acknowledged that technological progress and the expansion of digitalization in the field of labor law will inevitably lead to the emergence of new forms of employment. This, in turn, requires due attention from legislators to ensure the effective protection of labor rights and the provision of social guarantees to workers.

items.abstract: The objective of this research was to develop an ergonomic human-powered agricultural tool for soil tillage. The methodology comprised four stages: 1) selecting existing human-powered tillers used for land preparation, weeding, and cultivation; 2) designing and constructing a prototype based on the mechanical principles of the wheel and axle, wedge, and lever; 3) field testing the prototype; and 4) refining the tool based on ergonomic indicators. The results indicated that the hoe was the most commonly used traditional tool among farmers, which was subsequently developed into the prototype by integrating the three aforementioned mechanical principles. This integration effectively improved soil structure by crushing small stones and clods, thereby reducing the farmers' physical workload. Ergonomic assessment involved 25 parameters based on human-tool interaction, categorized into four body regions: the wrist, lower arm, upper arm, and trunk. Regarding the mechanical advantage (M.A.) of the developed tool, the values were recorded as 0.415 and 0.616 for general use and pulling, respectively. Notably, the mechanical advantage during the pushing phase reached 3.286, while other configurations yielded M.A. values of 1.85 (pushing) and 0.515 (pulling). The development of this ergonomic tiller significantly minimizes physical strain and operational time, allowing farmers to work longer and more efficiently. The application of the wheel, axle, and wedge systems to enhance mechanical advantage is a crucial factor in transitioning from labor-intensive farming to tool-assisted agriculture, ultimately leading to increased productivity and higher income for farmers.

items.abstract: This academic article aims to examine and synthesize knowledge concerning factors influencing the travel intentions of working-age adults. This is accomplished by reviewing, analyzing, and synthesizing relevant domestic and international research on travel behavior, travel motivation, and the influence of social media on travel decisions. The study found that the key factors associated with working adults’ travel intentions include intrinsic motivation and the perception of TikTok media. Intrinsic motivation serves as a fundamental driving force arising from individuals’ needs, interests, and personal satisfaction, thereby playing a significant role in shaping travel intentions and l decision-making. Meanwhile, the perception of TikTok content involves both cognitive and emotional processing. The platform’s distinctive features, including short-form video content, entertainment, and the presentation of travel experiences, can enhance users’ cognitive responses, attitudes, and behavioral intentions. Together, these two factors influence the travel intentions of working adults. Thus, working adults’ travel intentions are not shaped solely by media influence; rather, they result from the systematic interplay between individuals’ intrinsic motivation and their perception of TikTok content.

items.abstract: 要旨(日本語) 近年、人工知能(AI)や無人自律システムの進展に伴い、標的の選定や殺傷の判断を機械に委ねる「自動化された戦争(オート戦争)」および自律型致死兵器システム(LAWS)の配備を推進する議論が見られる。推進派は兵士の人的被害低減や戦闘判断の超高速化を利点として挙げるが、これらは軍事技術の不確実性と国際人道法の規範を軽視した技術決定論的過信である。 本稿では、「オート戦争」構想が孕む3つの本質的リスクを批判的に検討する。 1. アルゴリズムの暴走と誤認:AIのハルシネーション(誤判断)や戦場での通信途絶下において、人間の介入なしに暴走を制止できない危険性。 2. 高速エスカレーションの誘発:機械同士の応答連鎖が人間の意思決定速度を超越し、瞬間的かつ破滅的な事態(フラッシュ・ウォー)を招くリスク。 3. 責任の所在の喪失(責任の空白):過誤発生時に機械へ法的・倫理的責任を問うことはできず、国際人道法上の処罰および抑止機能が形骸化する問題。 分析の結果、生死を左右する武力行使において「有意義な人間の関与(Meaningful Human Control: MHC)」の維持が不可欠であると結論付け、国際的拘束力を持つ規制枠組みの早期確立を提言する。 Abstract (English) With recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and autonomous systems, advocacy for "automated warfare"—delegating lethal target selection and engagement decisions to autonomous machines—has gained traction. Proponents often cite the reduction of human soldier casualties and rapid computational processing as key operational benefits. However, this perspective reflects a techno-deterministic optimism that underestimates technical vulnerabilities and fundamentally challenges international humanitarian law (IHL). This paper critically examines three structural risks inherent in fully automated warfare: 1. Algorithmic Failure and Misidentification: The lack of human fail-safes during algorithmic hallucinations or communication cutoffs under hostile electronic warfare conditions. 2. Hyper-Velocity Escalation: The risk of uncontrollable, compounding engagement loops ("flash wars") that exceed human cognitive response times. 3. Erosion of Accountability: The emergence of a "responsibility gap" where machines cannot be held legally or morally liable, undermining the core deterrence mechanisms of IHL. The paper concludes that preserving Meaningful Human Control (MHC) over lethal decisions is a moral and legal imperative, urging the international community to establish legally binding regulatory frameworks against fully autonomous weapon systems.

items.abstract: 要旨(日本語) 近年、人工知能(AI)や無人自律システムの進展に伴い、標的の選定や殺傷の判断を機械に委ねる「自動化された戦争(オート戦争)」および自律型致死兵器システム(LAWS)の配備を推進する議論が見られる。推進派は兵士の人的被害低減や戦闘判断の超高速化を利点として挙げるが、これらは軍事技術の不確実性と国際人道法の規範を軽視した技術決定論的過信である。 本稿では、「オート戦争」構想が孕む3つの本質的リスクを批判的に検討する。 1. アルゴリズムの暴走と誤認:AIのハルシネーション(誤判断)や戦場での通信途絶下において、人間の介入なしに暴走を制止できない危険性。 2. 高速エスカレーションの誘発:機械同士の応答連鎖が人間の意思決定速度を超越し、瞬間的かつ破滅的な事態(フラッシュ・ウォー)を招くリスク。 3. 責任の所在の喪失(責任の空白):過誤発生時に機械へ法的・倫理的責任を問うことはできず、国際人道法上の処罰および抑止機能が形骸化する問題。 分析の結果、生死を左右する武力行使において「有意義な人間の関与(Meaningful Human Control: MHC)」の維持が不可欠であると結論付け、国際的拘束力を持つ規制枠組みの早期確立を提言する。 Abstract (English) With recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and autonomous systems, advocacy for "automated warfare"—delegating lethal target selection and engagement decisions to autonomous machines—has gained traction. Proponents often cite the reduction of human soldier casualties and rapid computational processing as key operational benefits. However, this perspective reflects a techno-deterministic optimism that underestimates technical vulnerabilities and fundamentally challenges international humanitarian law (IHL). This paper critically examines three structural risks inherent in fully automated warfare: 1. Algorithmic Failure and Misidentification: The lack of human fail-safes during algorithmic hallucinations or communication cutoffs under hostile electronic warfare conditions. 2. Hyper-Velocity Escalation: The risk of uncontrollable, compounding engagement loops ("flash wars") that exceed human cognitive response times. 3. Erosion of Accountability: The emergence of a "responsibility gap" where machines cannot be held legally or morally liable, undermining the core deterrence mechanisms of IHL. The paper concludes that preserving Meaningful Human Control (MHC) over lethal decisions is a moral and legal imperative, urging the international community to establish legally binding regulatory frameworks against fully autonomous weapon systems.

items.title: (Repositioning) AI as trickster in organizations for bias mitigation
items.abstract: As a contribution to the ongoing discussions on artificial intelligence (AI) ethics, I propose a feminist way of thinking on the positioning of AI in organizations. Inspired by the trickster figure that originates in mythology and folklore, I develop the notion of ‘trickster AI’ to conceptualize the fluid, relational, and ambivalent role of AI in organizational contexts. The ‘trickster AI’ is further supported by an empirical study drawing on a series of co-creation workshops on AI design for bias mitigation in hiring. Four AI-based solutions from the workshop – neutralization , standardization , customization , and diversification – are identified and analysed to examine how different configurations of AI and human actors shape the construction of bias and fairness. Rather than treating AI as inherently fair or biased, the findings show how the role of AI is continuously negotiated and reconfigured across practices. Interpreting these configurations through the lens of the trickster, the article highlights AI’s fluid positionality, inherent ambivalence, and capacity for boundary crossing. It contributes to feminist organization studies and feminist approaches to AI by moving beyond binary understandings of technology and foregrounding the situated, relational, and multiple enactments of fairness in sociotechnical practices.

items.abstract: This presentation summarizes the 90 Days of Research Visibility® initiative, a practical framework that shows researchers how to use artificial intelligence (AI) to build a consistent, authentic, and discoverable personal research presence. It highlights practical approaches for strengthening academic identity and digital presence, transforming research publications into engaging content, and communicating research effectively to audiences beyond academia. The presentation also examines how AI-assisted tools can help researchers improve research discoverability, visibility, engagement, and overall impact across academic and professional platforms. Drawing on lessons and practical activities from the 90-day initiative, the session provides an accessible roadmap for researchers and faculty members to integrate AI into their research communication and visibility workflows while maintaining human judgment, authenticity, and academic integrity.

items.title: A Cadaveric Study of Morphological Variations of the Abductor Pollicis Longus Muscle and Its Tendinous Insertions.
items.abstract: This study examined the abductor pollicis longus (APL) and abductor pollicis brevis (APB) muscles, which are key muscles involved in thumb abduction and fine motor function, with anatomical variations of the APL particularly accessory tendons implicated in the pathogenesis of De Quervain's tenosynovitis by contributing to crowding within the first dorsal compartment. This cadaveric observational study was conducted at the Department of Anatomy in collaboration with the Department of Physiology, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Gorakhpur, India, using twenty prosected upper limbs from voluntarily donated cadavers of Indian origin (10 rights and 10 lefts). Morphological parameters recorded included tendon length, width, attachment patterns, presence of accessory APL (a-APL) and APB variations, while biomechanical measurements included fascicle length, pennation angle and muscle mass, with physiological cross-sectional area (PCSA) and maximum force (Fmax) calculated using standard biomechanical formulas. All 20 specimens demonstrated a normal APL muscle belly and tendon; accessory APL tendons were identified in 70.0% of specimens, with 8 right-sided and 6 left-sided occurrences. Mean ±SD tendon length of APL was 62.8±17.41 mm on the right and 71.0±19.84 mm on the left, while mean width was 2.3±0.59 mm and 2.6±0.52 mm, respectively. A rare anatomical variation was observed in one specimen where APB originated from the accessory APL tendon. Biomechanical analysis showed APL had a PCSA of 3.27 cm² and predicted Fmax of 114.45 N, whereas APB demonstrated a PCSA of 1.42 cm² and Fmax of 49.70 N. These findings confirm that accessory APL tendons and atypical APB origins are common anatomical variants with significant clinical implications in De Quervain's tenosynovitis and that integration of morphometric and biomechanical data can enhance surgical decompression strategies, rehabilitation planning, ergonomic counseling and evidence-based nursing care.

items.title: A cautionary tale on the cost-effectiveness of collaborative AI in real-world medical applications
items.abstract: Abstract Federated learning (FL) has gained wide popularity as a collaborative learning paradigm allowing collaborative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in sensitive healthcare applications. Nevertheless, the practical implementation of FL presents technical and organizational challenges, as it generally requires complex communication infrastructures. In this context, consensus-based learning (CBL) may represent a promising alternative for collaborative learning, allowing the combination of local knowledge into a federated decision system, while potentially reducing deployment overhead. Nevertheless, a comprehensive assessment of the viability of consensus-based learning as a cost-effective and sustainable alternative to federated learning has not yet been conducted. In this work we propose an extensive benchmark of the accuracy, cost-effectiveness, and sustainability of a panel of FL and CBL methods in a wide range of collaborative medical data analysis scenarios. The benchmark includes 7 different medical datasets, encompassing 3 machine learning tasks, 8 different data modalities, and multi-centric settings involving 3 to 23 clients. Our results reveal that CBL is a cost-effective and more sustainable alternative to FL. When compared across the panel of medical datasets in the considered benchmark, CBL methods provide equivalent accuracy to the one achieved by FL. Nonetheless, CBL significantly reduces training time and communication cost (resp. 15 fold and 131 fold decrease) ( p -value< 0.05). This study opens a novel perspective on the deployment of collaborative AI in real-world applications, whereas the adoption of cost-effective methods is instrumental to achieve sustainability and democratization of AI by alleviating the need for extensive computational resources.

items.title: A Citation-Grounded Benchmark for Trustworthy Earnings Call Transcript Analysis with Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly used for financial document analysis, including earnings call transcripts (ECTs). Beyond generating standalone claims, users increasingly prefer grounded analyses that pair claims with verifiable citations from source documents to enable independent validation. However, evaluating such analytical claims typically requires extensive expert annotation, which is costly and difficult to scale, and real-world financial analysis commonly involves long context-question-answer triplets, further increasing task complexity. To address these challenges and benchmark the current landscape of grounded analysis by LLMs, we propose a numeric evidence evaluation method that enables groundedness assessment without reliance on expert annotation. We also introduce an automated dataset construction pipeline and construct ECTs-100 from the top 100 constituents of the S&P 500 to support benchmark of both groundedness and correctness. In addition, we examine conscious incompetence, a practical failure mode in financial analysis in which LLMs must detect when available evidence is insufficient and refrain from producing unsupported hallucinations. Empirical results show that LLMs perform well in groundedness but face notable limitations in correctness, with informational insufficiency presenting an additional challenge.

items.title: A Community-centered Vision for Data-Intensive Great Lakes Research and Management
items.abstract: Abstract The Laurentian Great Lakes are a vital freshwater resource and a regionally significant natural system facing complex, persistent, and compounding challenges from climate change, nutrient loading, and invasive species. The increasing availability of observational data, coupled with advances in computational power and machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) methods, presents an opportunity to address these challenges by improving data integration and enabling powerful data-driven models. This perspective article outlines a broad vision for applying AI in Great Lakes research and management. We review the current state of AI efforts across several key topic areas and propose a cross-disciplinary roadmap focused on advanced modeling, multi-modal data fusion, and operational forecasting. Realizing this vision will require sustained investment in open data infrastructure, shared computational resources, and inter-institutional collaboration. If successful, this roadmap will accelerate research progress, improve decision-support tools, and enhance the resilience and sustainability of the region’s interconnected ecological and economic foundations.
